subject: SOC 2 audit window alignment and sub-service evidence ask
thread_messages:
From: Robert Pena <robert.pena@brightpathaudits.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Liz March <liz@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SOC 2 coverage / subservice confirmation

Hi Jordan —

Aurora's audit team is consolidating vendor evidence for our SOC 2 Type II planning. A couple quick clarifications on Redwood's coverage would help us:

1) For your hosted offering, do you publish a SOC 2 Type II for Redwood as a whole, or do you rely on cloud provider reports with a carve-out? If the latter, do you provide a bridge/letter that maps our expected audit window to the cloud provider's reporting period?

2) We need a clear list of subprocessors and any evidence we can provide to our auditor that delineates shared responsibility boundaries (network controls, encryption at rest, key management).

Can you confirm what you can share by EOD Monday (US time)?

Thanks,
Robert
Robert Pena
Senior Auditor, BrightPath Audits
robert.pena@brightpathaudits.com

-----
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Robert Pena <robert.pena@brightpathaudits.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Liz March <liz@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SOC 2 coverage / subservice confirmation

Robert —

Thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers up front:
- Redwood maintains an in-scope SOC 2 Type II (security + availability) covering our control environment for the hosted API.
- For our cloud infrastructure components we operate as a carve-out: we rely on our cloud provider's SOC 2 for that underlying infrastructure, and we produce a bridge letter that maps control ownership across the audit window.

What I can provide this week:
- Subservice mapping PDF that shows which controls are Redwood-managed vs cloud-managed (attachment: redwood_subservice_map.pdf).
- Subprocessor inventory (csv) with contracts and data access descriptions (attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv).
- A draft bridge-letter template we routinely share (bridge_letter_template.docx).

Marissa (security/compliance) will add detail on specific artifacts auditors typically accept and propose dates to align audit windows. Karthik will help confirm any outstanding evidence tied to networking and KMS.

Are there any specific audit dates your team is targeting for Aurora (start of testing / control period)? If you share your audit window we can generate an explicit statement mapping Redwood's evidence to your dates.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>; Robert Pena <robert.pena@brightpathaudits.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Liz March <liz@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SOC 2 coverage / subservice confirmation

Hi Robert / Jordan / Liz —

Thanks for looping me in. A few specifics auditors commonly request and what we can provide:

Requested artifact -> Redwood deliverable (typical)
- Cloud provider SOC 2 (in-scope period) -> We provide the provider's SOC 2 report and a redwood-specific bridge letter mapping controls to our operating dates.
- Subprocessor contracts + data access matrix -> subprocessor_inventory.csv (names, function, access type, contract dates).
- Network segmentation diagrams and tenant isolation controls -> network_diagram_v2.pdf (we'll include in the Drive link).
- KMS/HSM evidence -> statement of key custody + KM integration logs (summary extract).
- Evidence of change control and deployment separation -> sample release pipeline run and PR approvals (redacted).

To be explicit on carve-out language: Redwood's cloud dependency is a carve-out of the provider's environment — we do not claim responsibility for provider-managed controls (physical access, hypervisor separation, etc.). Our bridge letter states this and maps Redwood's controls (application auth, token management, encryption keys at rest for customer-managed keys, logging/alerts) to the auditor's common criteria.

Proposed timeline for Aurora: if your control testing window is June 1 — Nov 30 2027, we can produce a dated bridge letter and assemble the evidence pack by May 24, 2027. If you need an earlier window, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Attachments I can share immediately (drive links included in the thread metadata): redwood_subservice_map.pdf, subprocessor_inventory.csv, bridge_letter_template.docx.

If BrightPath requires any additional attestation language, please share the exact wording and we can evaluate inclusion in the bridge letter (some auditors request specific phraseology around provider carve-outs).

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

-----
From: Robert Pena <robert.pena@brightpathaudits.com>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SOC 2 coverage / subservice confirmation

Marissa / Jordan —

Appreciate the quick rundown. That timeline works for Aurora's audit window (June through November). Please go ahead and upload the bridge letter draft to the Drive link and include the subprocessor csv.

Two small asks from BrightPath: 1) a short paragraph in the bridge letter that explicitly states which provider controls remain outside Redwood's scope (we'll share sample language if helpful), and 2) confirmation whether any subprocessors handle PHI for Aurora (Aurora has some PHI scope in their environment).

I'll confirm the auditor's exact testing start date once internal scheduling finalizes.

Thanks,
Robert
